body.heading: Where in the world is Germany?
paragraphs: Germany is a country in Western Europe, which is part of Europe.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Germany is Berlin.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Germany is German.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Germany is the euro. The euro is shared by many countries in Europe, so the same coins and notes work across borders.

body.heading: How big is Germany?
paragraphs: Germany covers about 357,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of France.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Neuschwanstein is the fairytale castle that inspired Disney's — white towers in the Alps above lakes and forest, built by a king who loved stories.
Berlin mixes world history and fun: the Brandenburg Gate, the East Side Gallery's painted wall, island museums and the TV Tower's spinning views.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Germany on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
